audit_result.proof_trace: The POST handler performs a non-atomic read-then-delete: `get_authorization_code` (L70-71) SELECTs the code from the database, then `delete_authorization_code` (L151-152) removes it only after token issuance — with at least one async DB round-trip (member query, L124-128) between the two RPCs. Under PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED isolation two concurrent requests can both SELECT the same code before either DELETE commits, and the delete result is silently discarded (no destructuring on L151-152), so both requests pass all in-memory validations and each receives a valid 30-day access token.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An attacker who controls an OAuth client (or intercepts an authorization code) fires two simultaneous POST /oauth/token requests with identical code, client_id, client_secret, code_verifier, and redirect_uri; both requests read the code before either deletes it, causing the server to issue two independent access tokens from a single authorization code.

PROP-stem-system-inv-002.text: Authorization code must be single-use; deleted immediately after successful token exchange.
